newsitem.title: CANADA: Falconbridge Dominican labor contract ends.
newsitem.headline: Falconbridge Dominican labor contract ends.

text.p: Falconbridge Ltd said on Monday that its contract with about 1,000 unionized workers in the Dominican Republic has expired but the employees are not yet in a strike position.
The three-year agreement at Falconbridge Dominicana ended on Saturday, Falconbridge spokeswoman Caroline Casselman told Reuters.
Dominican rules require a mandatory period of conciliation before a strike or lockout are allowed, she said, noting, "They haven't even asked for conciliation at this point."
Management and the union will continue to negotiate throughout December, but talks are slowing down because of Christmas, Cassleman said.
"My understanding is there won't be an awful lot happening between now and January."
In 1995, the facility produced 30,900 tonnes of nickel in ferronickel. The plant employs a total of 1,500 workers.
